crossRefs.note: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith who made silver shrines of Artemis, brought no little business to the…
But when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If indeed it were a matter of wrong or of wicked…
If there arises a matter too hard for you in judgment, between blood and blood, between plea and plea, and between…
Dare any of you, having a matter against his neighbor, go to law before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?

people.name: Demetrius
people.line: Silversmith who opposed Paul in Ephesus

translations.web: If therefore Demetrius and the craftsmen who are with him have a matter against anyone, the courts are open, and there are proconsuls. Let them press charges against one another.
translations.bsb: So if Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open and proconsuls are available. Let them bring charges against one another there.
translations.kjv: Wherefore if Demetrius, and the craftsmen which are with him, have a matter against any man, the law is open, and there are deputies: let them implead one another.
translations.asv: If therefore Demetrius, and the craftsmen that are with him, have a matter against any man, the courts are open, and there are proconsuls: let them accuse one another.
